expected_evidence: Geological: anomalous platinum (and iridium/platinum-group-element) concentration spikes in a discrete stratigraphic layer at the Younger Dryas onset (~12,800 cal BP), detectable in ice cores (e.g., Greenland GISP2/GRIP) and in lake/peat/loess sediment sequences.

Astronomical/impact-proxy markers co-occurring with the platinum spike: magnetic microspherules, nanodiamonds (lonsdaleite/cubic diamond), melt-glass, and elevated iridium — used as corroborating impact-ejecta signatures.
Material/archaeological: a 'black mat' or charcoal-rich horizon at multiple North American and Eurasian sites marking abrupt faunal/cultural discontinuity coincident with the platinum layer.

Cross-continental replication: matching platinum anomaly timing and magnitude at geographically dispersed sites (e.g., North America, Greenland ice core, Western Europe, and potentially the Levant/Syria) needed to support the 'multiple-continents' claim.
Genetic: possible megafaunal population bottleneck/extinction signatures in ancient DNA dated to the same interval, though this is an indirect and weaker line of evidence.
Absence expected for textual, linguistic, oral-tradition, and iconographic evidence, since no literate or narrative-recording cultures existed in this pre-Holocene interval.
response.rationale: The hypothesis falls squarely in the Younger Dryas period/interval, and its core claim (a corroborated platinum anomaly across multiple continents from impact-ejecta fallout) is precisely the kind of signal captured by geological (0.65) and astronomical/impact-proxy (0.7) detectability channels, which are the highest-detectability rows available for this period — ice cores and fine-grained sediment sequences are known to preserve chemostratigraphic anomalies over 10,000+ years with reasonably good fidelity. Material evidence (black mat horizons, 0.35) offers weaker but plausible corroboration. Textual (0.0), linguistic (0.05), oral_tradition (0.1), and iconographic (0.1) channels are essentially inert for a pre-literate, pre-narrative-recording interval, so their absence is fully expected and uninformative about truth or falsity. Genetic evidence (0.3) is indirect at best (megafaunal bottlenecks, not human genetic signal). Given that geological/astronomical evidence — the most relevant channels — have moderate-to-good detectability (0.6–0.7) and, per model-prior, published literature (Firestone et al. 2007; Petaev et al. 2013; Moore et al. 2017; Wittke et al. 2013) does report platinum/PGE anomalies at multiple globally dispersed sites at this boundary (though causal interpretation as impact-driven remains scientifically contested), the hypothesis is falsifiable and testable, and any absence of evidence in the low-detectability channels (textual, linguistic, oral tradition, iconographic) should not be taken as evidence against it. I flag the causal 'impact-ejecta' mechanism attribution as unverified model-prior recollection rather than settled fact, since the platinum-anomaly observation itself is more robustly established in the literature than its interpretation as extraterrestrial impact ejecta versus alternative terrestrial/volcanic or reworking explanations.
